explanation: Store unmatched opening-parenthesis indices and a separate index end for the latest unmatched closing parenthesis. A matched close pops one opening; the next stack top or end marks the boundary before the longest balanced suffix.
timeComplexity: O(n) Each character pushes or pops at most one index.
spaceComplexity: O(n) An all-opening string leaves n unmatched indices on the stack.
attribution: Unmodified EPIJudge reference source: epi_judge_java_solutions/epi/LongestSubstringWithMatchingParentheses.java. Original contributors; repository LICENSE: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc-nd/4.0/).
correctness: Unmatched openings and the latest unmatched close are exactly the barriers a balanced suffix cannot cross. After a matching close, every character since the nearest remaining barrier is balanced. Its length is currentIndex−barrier, and checking every closing position covers every possible optimal substring.
walkthrough: For ")()(()", the leading close sets the invalid-prefix boundary. The following () gives length 2. The trailing (() contains another matched pair of length 2, so the answer remains 2.
edgeCases: An unmatched closing parenthesis resets the base boundary.
Unmatched openings separate possible balanced suffixes.
